speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding gums, and a rash of tiny red spots on your skin. To understand the cause of this bleeding, have you been bruising easily or had excessive bleeding after any recent cuts?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP).

The combination of frequent epistaxis, gum bleeding, petechiae on the extremities, and easy bruising in a 4-year-old is classic for ITP. Have there been any recent viral infections or fever in the past month? REQUEST IMAGES: Skin exam showing petechiae and ecchymoses.
